title: Annotate your own game before the engine
outcomes: Marks at most three critical moments in his own game, with what he saw, expected and planned, before consulting an engine
Uses routine, slip and blunder bands to compare his marks with an engine's measurement
Separates where a game turned from why it turned, and asks tentative questions about the why

steps.text: **Annotate before the engine.** An engine says what was best. Only you know what you saw. After a game, replay it and mark at most three **critical moments**: where you were unsure, thought a long time, were surprised, or changed your plan. For each, write what you saw, what you expected and what you planned. Only then ask an engine.

steps.prompt: Think of your last game. Before looking anything up, write down up to three moments you would mark. For each: what did you see, what did you expect your opponent to do, and what was your plan?

steps.text: To check your marks, use three bands for what a move cost, measured by an engine at a fixed depth: **routine** (many moves about as good), **slip** (costs half a pawn to a pawn and a half), **blunder** (costs two pawns or more). The cut-offs are my own choice, not a law, and a move that falls between two bands is simply in between. The bands are a measuring stick for the move, not a verdict on you.

steps.caption: A sample game, up to White's sixth move. Where would you mark a critical moment? Decide before you open the next step.

steps.text: Now ask what happened at each swing, **tentatively**: (1) you did not see it; (2) you saw it but calculated wrongly; (3) you judged the resulting position wrongly; (4) the clock decided; (5) you were out of your opening knowledge. The engine can show where the swing is. Only you can say which of the five it was. Write the question you would ask yourself, not a verdict.

steps.prompt: Take one of the moments you marked at the start. Which of the five questions fits it best, and what could you check in the game to find out?

Look at the three moments you marked at the start. Which one are you least sure is the real turning point, and what in the game would you check to decide? Write low, medium or high for how sure you are.
